To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Hypoxia increases the toxicity of PRIMA-1 in breast cancer cell models, irrespective of p 53 status.
hypoxia, a feature of the tumor microenviroment, sensitizes breast carcinoma cells to lower concentrations of PRIMA-1, irrespective of pS3 status, through a mechanism involving MnSOD and H2O2.
PRIMA- 1 is more effective against human breast cancer cells under hypoxia, and this may be related to the modulation of p53 conformation, and the increased oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel therapeutic targets in breast cancer and other malignancies.
developing novel therapeutic strategies to overcome tumor adaptation to hypoxic conditions and to restore p53 function.
understanding the role of hypoxia, MnSOD and H2O2 on p53 reactivation by PRIMA-1 in human breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hypoxia-induced increase in PRIMA-1 sensitivity is not due to the reactivation of mutant p53.
hypoxia, Mn SOD and H(20)(2) regulate p 53 reactivation and toxicity of PRIMA-1, irrespective of p 53 status in human cancer cells.
hypoxia, MnSOD and H(20)2 regulate p53 re-activation and PRIMA toxicity irrespective of p-53 status in human mammary carcinoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypoxia, MnSOD and H( 2)O( 2) regulate p 53 reactivation and toxicity of PRIMA-1 irrespective of p 53 status in human mammary cancer cells.
PRIMA- 1 is a promising anticancer agent, especially for tumors with mutant p53, but it may also be effective for p53 wt tumors under hypoxic conditions.
PRIMA- 1 toxicity is regulated by hypoxia, Mn- SOD and H( 2)O( 2) irrespective of p53 mutation status in human breast carcinoma cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PRIMA- 1 is effective under hypoxia and that hypoxia can be used to sensitize cancer cells to PRIMA 1, irrespective of p 53 status.
hypoxia can be a major determinant of the response of cancer cells to PRIMA, irrespective of the p53 status.
hypoxia is part and parcel of the tumor micro-environment favoring tumor adaptation and resistance to chemotherapy, irrespective of p 53 status.
